I'm now settling on whether xanthoma counts. It's a named skin lesion with its own place in MeSH under skin diseases, so I'll annotate it as a SpecificDisease, even though it's really a manifestation of CTX.

content.text: {"decisions":[{"id":1,"entity":"SpecificDisease","rationale":"\"cerebrotendinous xanthomatosis\" names one specific disease (CTX) with a single definition, so it is annotated as a Specific Disease with the full span preferred.","guideline_section":"What to Annotate 1 (Specific Disease); What to Annotate 5 (minimum necessary span)"},{"id":2,"entity":"SpecificDisease","rationale":"Second occurrence of the same specific disease name in the abstract; duplicate mentions are annotated separately.","guideline_section":"What to Annotate 4 (Annotate duplicate mentions)"},{"id":3,"entity":"SpecificDisease","rationale":"\"CTX\" is the abbreviation defined for cerebrotendinous xanthomatosis; the short form is annotated as its own mention, separate from the long form.","guideline_section":"What to Annotate 6 (Annotate all synonymous mentions)"},{"id":4,"entity":"SpecificDisease","rationale":"Second occurrence of the abbreviation CTX, which refers to the same specific disease and is annotated as a duplicate mention.","guideline_section":"What to Annotate 4 (Annotate duplicate mentions); What to Annotate 6 (synonymous mentions)"},{"id":5,"entity":"NONE","rationale":"\"disease\" in \"progression of disease\" is a very general term that does not name a specific disease or disease class, so it is excluded.","guideline_section":"What NOT to Annotate 4 (Do not annotate general terms)"},{"id":6,"entity":"SpecificDisease","rationale":"\"xanthoma\" is a distinct, named pathological skin lesion linkable to one specific definition, so it is treated as a specific disease mention rather than a general term; it is listed as a clinical manifestation of CTX.","guideline_section":"What to Annotate 1 (Specific Disease)"}]}
